scores.evidence: Phase 3: "Depends on: V1, Phase 2 (repo retrieval), V2 before any repo code runs."
scores.rationale: Phases go skeleton → defenses → triage → sandbox → live resolution → widening, with each phase listing proven dependencies and gates.

scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real production end-to-end slice through 8 tiers, deployed, traced and rolled back, before any features.

scores.evidence: Flip condition: "V1 fails → suggestions go only to a maintainer dashboard, with no public writes"
scores.rationale: The gate table gives reversibility, default, assumption, validation and flip condition for each irreversible decision, and the missing inputs are stated explicitly.

scores.evidence: Phase 1 tasks: policy executor and approval binding first, then redaction, budgets, then shadow triage; Phase 3 sandbox before coding loop.
scores.rationale: Within phases the cross-cutting gates (executor, approvals, isolation) come before narrower leaf work, and rollout is one repo, then more.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: "Minimal App permissions on one repo; HMAC check; secrets in a secret manager; untrusted-data block; author allow-list; kill switch"
scores.rationale: Each phase from 0 to 5 has concrete security controls.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: "One OpenTelemetry trace per run across all tiers; token and cost metrics; DLQ and error alerts"
scores.rationale: Observability is concrete in Phase 0 and in every later phase.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: "IaC; image digest, model ID and prompt version stamped on every run"
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is addressed in every phase: pinned digests, versioned evals, fixed replay inputs.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: "Idempotency on the delivery ID; DLQ; model-call timeout; rollback to the previous digest"
scores.rationale: Each phase has failure handling: a reconciliation sweep, fallback model, TTL reaper, PR caps and quality breakers.

scores.evidence: Sublayer table: injection defense (0,1), budgets (0,1), HITL (1), retrieval (2), model access, memory (2), orchestration (3), routing (2), feedback (5)
scores.rationale: Defenses, budgets and human gating come before capabilities, then retrieval → model → memory → orchestration → routing → feedback. Routing is built in Phase 2, slightly out of order relative to orchestration in Phase 3, but it is fixed-by-task and dynamic routing is deferred.

scores.evidence: "Auto-merge of agent PRs. Pulled forward if, for one narrow change class, V5's merged-with-minor-edits rate stays high over ≥ 100 PRs"
scores.rationale: Each deferred item has a concrete pull-forward condition.

note: Exceptionally thorough plan that meets every rubric dimension with concrete content; the only quibble is that routing is built before orchestration.
